The Trial Balance of 2024-25 lists the old, mostly uncoded accounts; the rules at the bottom say, account by account, which line of the statements each one feeds (the accounts of the new chart that the main mapping already claims are not repeated). party_text: Zoho's Trial Balance gives these accounts (advances to suppliers and others, trade payables, retention money and outstanding expenses) only as one net figure. The signed statements split it by supplier from the supplier ledgers, which are read for the current year only. The net is compared; the sections' totals leave the group out on both sides.
explain_note: The differences in revenue, purchases and other expenses cancel out in profit: profit before tax differs by only ₹3. The signed statements appear to set about ₹3.64 lakh of income against expenses and to show ₹34,517 of expenses under purchases, while Zoho keeps them as they were booked. The entries cannot be identified from the Trial Balance, so nothing is changed or asked for.

explain.text: Zoho shows ₹3,63,999 more revenue than the signed statement.
The same ₹3,63,999 as in revenue from operations.
Zoho shows ₹34,517 less under purchases than the signed statement.
Zoho shows ₹3,98,517 more under other expenses than the signed statement.
The net of the differences in purchases and other expenses. It equals the difference in revenue, so profit agrees.
